---
title: Differentiability
---

A Laplace approximation is a function of the parameters $\theta$ it is fitted at.
Its curvature, its log marginal likelihood and its predictive all depend on $\theta$, and some uses need their gradients.
For example, marginal-likelihood training of the network (Immer et al., 2021)[^immer2021] differentiates the log marginal likelihood with respect to $\theta$.
So **laplacekit** keeps two modes apart.

## The front door detaches

`lk.laplace` fits for the user, who wants numbers.
It detaches the chosen parameters, runs the fit loop under `torch.no_grad`, detaches the result, and gives the posterior its own copy of the mean.
Nothing it returns is attached to the user's autograd graph, and training the module afterwards doesn't move the posterior.

## By hand, the curvature stays differentiable

The steps that `lk.laplace` composes don't detach the params.
The curvature part of the statistic, the operator, the posterior and its mean keep their graph to `params`.
So do the log-determinant and prior terms of `neg_log_marglik`.

The one exception is the data-fit term.
The fold computes the log-likelihood under `no_grad`, so `stat.data_fit` is a plain value.
To get the gradient of the whole objective, we add the log-likelihood back from a forward pass of our own.
This leaves the objective's value unchanged:

```python
params = lk.subsets.last_layer(fn, caps)
fit = lk.core.fit_curvature(fn, lik, params, lk.DenseGGN(), capabilities=caps)
stat = fit.update(fit.init(), batch)
post = fit.posterior(fit.finalize(stat), prior=prior, n_data=stat.count)

log_lik = lk.core.log_prob(lik, fn(params, batch.inputs), batch.targets).sum()
post = copy.replace(post, data_fit=(stat.data_fit,))
loss = lk.objectives.neg_log_marglik(post) + stat.data_fit - log_lik
grads = torch.autograd.grad(loss, list(params.values()))
```

Without the last two terms of `loss`, `grads` would miss the gradient of the log-likelihood.
[Step by step](../examples/by_hand.py#gradients) runs this on a real model.

## What a plugin must do

A plugin's code runs in both modes, so it must not choose for the user.
In `update`, `finalize`, a prior's `log_prob`, a predictive or an objective, use

- no `.detach()`, `torch.no_grad()` or `.item()` on anything that depends on the params or on a hyperparameter;
- no round trip through NumPy or Python floats in the math.

This costs nothing in the front door, since its `no_grad` turns all of it into plain tensor arithmetic anyway.
Tensors that never depend on the params (sign vectors, masks, counts) are fine as they are.

Objectives have one more rule.
`lk.Minimize` minimizes them over the logs of the hyperparameters with L-BFGS, so they must be differentiable in those hyperparameters.
`lk.testing.check_objective` checks that a finite gradient reaches every hyperparameter of the posterior.
The [Tuning objectives](objective.py) guide shows an objective whose gradient flows through `lk.predict`.

[^immer2021]: Immer, A., Bauer, M., Fortuin, V., Rätsch, G., & Khan, M. E. (2021). Scalable marginal likelihood estimation for model selection in deep learning. *ICML*. <https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.04975>
